title: Fixed plans, source-qualified evidence and MCP compatibility

tests.name: test/contracts/unified-engine.test.js
tests.detail: 6/6: byte-span to line conversion including multi-byte text; method and kind narrowing onto the product enum; a real search returning anchored evidence; the language-server refusal reason; anchored semantic evidence with a configured server

tests.name: scripts/compatibility.mjs (both modes)
tests.detail: search, architecture, impact, references, symbol, restart and warm search over one code_intel tool in legacy and in unified mode

findings: One MCP tool, one response schema, existing metadata keys intact. Neither reader is visible to the caller.
Byte spans are authoritative and lines are derived by counting newlines; when a file cannot be read the evidence keeps its text and loses its locator rather than carrying a guessed line.
The control plane's six evidence methods narrow onto the product's three without inventing a stronger claim: a lexical hit never becomes an LSP fact.

Measured on the same two-file workspace and the same model, warm search went from 1812 ms (legacy) to 216 ms (unified); first search 7972 ms to 6284 ms; restart-first 2607 ms to 1889 ms. One sample each, not a benchmark distribution.
knownLimitations: The unified reader is selectable, not default.
rollback: Unset LAZY_INTEL_ENGINE and restart. No state migration.
